title: Tax Refund Advances: What They Really Cost

lines.say: Refund advances are everywhere in February. Some are fine. Some cost far more than they look. Let's run the numbers.
Here's the idea. A tax preparer or lender gives you part of your refund now, often a few hundred to a few thousand dollars, and gets paid back when your refund arrives.
Many advances advertise zero percent. But they often come with conditions: paying for tax prep, a fee to route your refund through their bank, or your money loaded onto their prepaid card.
So the advance can be free, while the package around it isn't.
Here's what a small fee really means.

scene.label: A $40 fee for $1,000, three weeks early
scene.sub: as a yearly rate: about three times a typical credit card

lines.cap: Say you pay a $40 fee to get $1,000 about three weeks early. As a yearly rate, that's roughly 70%.
lines.say: Say you pay a forty dollar fee to get a thousand dollars about three weeks early. As a yearly rate, that's roughly seventy percent.

scene.sub: The real cost of a "free" advance
scene.foot: $190 to get your own money ~3 weeks sooner

lines.cap: And if it also means paying $150 for tax prep you could have done free, the real cost of the advance is $190.
lines.say: And if the package also means paying a hundred fifty for tax prep you could have done for free, the real cost of the advance is a hundred and ninety dollars.

scene.text: E-file + direct deposit: most refunds in under 21 days.

lines.cap: The IRS says most refunds from e-filed returns with direct deposit arrive within 21 days. That's the same few weeks the advance is selling.
lines.say: The IRS says most refunds from e-filed returns with direct deposit arrive within twenty-one days. That's the same few weeks the advance is selling.

scene.head: BEFORE YOU TAKE AN ADVANCE
items: Can you file free? (IRS Free File, VITA)
Add up the total cost, not just the rate
Already gave the refund a job? (Ep. 13)

lines.say: So before you take one, check four things.
Can you file for free? If your income qualifies, IRS Free File and free VITA tax help exist for exactly this.
If you still want an advance, add up every fee, not just the advertised rate.
And decide your refund's job before it lands. Episode thirteen has the four questions.
